title: VP versus VBP over the complex numbers
formal: Is \(\mathrm{VP}_{\mathbb C}=\mathrm{VBP}_{\mathbb C}\)? More explicitly, let \((m_n,f_n)_{n\ge1}\) be any family with integers \(m_n\ge0\) and commutative polynomials \(f_n\in\mathbb C[x_1,\ldots,x_{m_n}]\). Suppose that some positive integer \(a\) satisfies \[m_n\le(n+2)^a,\qquad \deg f_n\le(n+2)^a,\qquad c(f_n)\le(n+2)^a\quad\text{for all }n\ge1,\] where \(c\) is minimum arithmetic-circuit size in the model below. Must there exist a positive integer \(b\), depending on the whole family, such that \[\operatorname{abp}(f_n)\le(n+2)^b\quad\text{for all }n\ge1?\] Computation is exact and nonuniform over the complex field, and the competing branching programs are unrestricted.
definitions:
A polynomial is a finite complex linear combination of commutative monomials in the listed variables. Its total degree is the maximum sum of exponents among nonzero monomials, with degree zero assigned to the zero polynomial. An arithmetic circuit is a finite acyclic graph with one designated output. Input gates are labelled by one listed variable or one arbitrary complex constant. Every other gate has two ordered input ports and is labelled by addition or multiplication in the polynomial ring; both ports may refer to the same predecessor, and any predecessor may be reused. There are no division gates. Size is the number of gates plus the number of wires, counting each input port’s wire separately; constant and variable input gates each have unit cost. Intermediate degrees are not separately bounded: the degree hypothesis is on the output polynomial after cancellations. The minimum of this size among circuits computing \(f\) is \(c(f)\).

An algebraic branching program (ABP) is a finite directed acyclic multigraph with distinct designated vertices \(s,t\), no edges entering \(s\), and no edges leaving \(t\). Each edge \(e\) is labelled by an affine form \(\lambda_e=\alpha_{e,0}+\sum_{j=1}^{m}\alpha_{e,j}x_j\), with arbitrary complex coefficients. It computes \(\sum_{\pi:s\leadsto t}\prod_{e\in\pi}\lambda_e\), where distinct paths include their edge choices and an empty sum is zero. Its size is \[|V|+|E|+\sum_{e\in E}\left(\mathbf1_{\alpha_{e,0}\ne0}+2\bigl|\{j\in[m]:\alpha_{e,j}\ne0\}\bigr|\right).\] Here \([m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}\), including the empty set if \(m=0\), and \(\mathbf1_P\) is one when \(P\) holds and zero otherwise. Thus every nonzero scalar coefficient and its variable occurrence are charged; labels are not arbitrary polynomial oracles. There is no width, layering, variable-order, read-once, syntactic multilinearity, symmetry, homogeneity or monotonicity requirement. The minimum size computing \(f\) is \(\operatorname{abp}(f)\).

Both minima concern formal polynomial identities, not agreement on finitely many inputs or convergence of coefficients. Sizes count algebraic objects and field elements, not bits encoding complex numbers; coefficients need not have bounded or computable bit descriptions. No algorithm generating a family’s circuits, programs or constants is required. Every polynomial has finite representations in both models. Positive integer exponents in \((n+2)^a\) absorb multiplicative constants and finitely many initial values of any polynomial bound. The families meeting the circuit hypotheses define \(\mathrm{VP}_{\mathbb C}\); polynomially many variables and a polynomial ABP bound define \(\mathrm{VBP}_{\mathbb C}\). ABP size already bounds output degree, and ABPs have polynomial-size circuit simulations, so only the displayed converse inclusion is at issue.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the displayed inclusion or its negation, with the specified field, polynomial identities, resource accounting and quantifiers. A positive proof establishes a polynomial ABP bound for every family satisfying the circuit and degree hypotheses; it need not produce an efficient uniform converter. A negative proof establishes one family \((m_n,f_n)\) and one fixed positive integer \(a\) satisfying all three circuit-side bounds, but such that \[\forall b\ge1\ \forall N\ge1\ \exists n\ge N,\quad \operatorname{abp}(f_n)>(n+2)^b.\] The lower bound must cover every permitted ABP over \(\mathbb C\), including arbitrary constants, reuse of variables and cancellations. There is no required effective generator for a separating family. A lower bound in a restricted ABP model, a family of exponential output degree, or a border-complexity separation does not meet this criterion.
why: The question compares unrestricted arithmetic circuits with path-sum computation inside the class of efficiently representable polynomials. Equality would make polynomial-size determinants of affine matrices sufficient to express every polynomial-degree circuit family. Inequality would establish a fundamental separation within efficient algebraic computation, isolating power supplied by general multiplication together with reuse of intermediate results.

importance.reason: A basic class equality linking general arithmetic circuits, algebraic branching programs and determinant universality; current symmetry and multilinearity results remain model-specific.

progress.text: Valiant, Skyum, Berkowitz and Rackoff establish classical depth reduction; the checked ITCS 2024 exposition records the resulting quasipolynomial equivalence of the algebraic models.
Sinhababu and Thierauf prove polynomial ABP factor closure over characteristic-zero fields at CCC.
The factor-closure result is published in Computational Complexity. It does not identify ABPs with general circuits.
Fabris, Limaye, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff study the power of min-partition rank for syntactically multilinear ABPs and recover a restricted formula–ABP separation.
Dwivedi, Pago and Seppelt post the symmetric-class separation and separate completeness results; the work appears at STOC 2026.
The revised factoring survey retains \(\mathrm{VF}\subseteq\mathrm{VBP}\subseteq\mathrm{VP}\) with no strict containment known, in Remark 7.3.

status_note: Open in the checked June 2026 factoring survey, Remark 7.3. Bounded searches and version checks through 15 September 2026 found no resolution for unrestricted commutative exact nonuniform computation over C. The January/June symmetry separation uses orbit complexity, prescribed variable symmetries and no degree bound; the multilinear report studies a syntactically restricted model; min-plus-semiring results have different operations. Characteristic-zero factor closure and quasipolynomial simulations do not imply the required polynomial simulation. Complete new proofs were not independently verified.

context_blocks.text: Circuits combine previously computed polynomials by both addition and multiplication, with unrestricted reuse. An ABP records sums of products along paths with affine labels. ABPs are polynomially equivalent to skew circuits, where each multiplication gate has at least one operand that is an input variable or constant. The conjectural gap concerns the size of exact representations under these two forms of computation, rather than which individual polynomials can be represented at all.

The polynomial-degree condition is essential. Small general circuits can have output degree exponential in their size, whereas an ABP with affine labels has degree at most its longest source-to-sink path. Such degree alone cannot separate the classes in this card because it is explicitly required to stay polynomial. The stated bounds concern the final polynomial; intermediate cancellations and degrees in a competing circuit are allowed.

Determinants give an equivalent structural description of \(\mathrm{VBP}\): a family belongs to this class exactly when it has representations \(f_n=\det(A_{n,0}+\sum_j x_j A_{n,j})\) with polynomially bounded matrix dimension and complex constant matrices. The determinant itself admits polynomial-size ABPs. Thus \(\mathrm{VP}=\mathrm{VBP}\) would make determinants universal for the circuit families in the statement. This is distinct from permanent versus determinant: the permanent is not known to have the polynomial-size general circuits required on the easy side of a separation here.

The classical Valiant–Skyum–Berkowitz–Rackoff depth reduction yields quasipolynomial simulations among formulas, ABPs and circuits for polynomial-degree families. The ITCS 2024 paper recalls that their quasipolynomial versions coincide, where a quasipolynomial bound means \(n^{(\log n)^{O(1)}}\). A polynomial bound \(n^{O(1)}\) is stronger. Approximation in coefficient space also defines separate border-complexity classes and does not supply an exact ABP identity.

Sinhababu and Thierauf prove factor closure over fields of characteristic zero: every factor of a nonzero polynomial with ABP size \(s\) has ABP size polynomial in \(s\). The result appeared at CCC 2020 and in Computational Complexity in October 2021. This gives ABPs a closure property already known for general circuits, without equating the models. The revised factoring survey of June 2026 still records that no inclusion in \(\mathrm{VF}\subseteq\mathrm{VBP}\subseteq\mathrm{VP}\) is known to be strict.

Dwivedi, Pago and Seppelt separate symmetric analogues of these three classes in their STOC 2026 work. Three differences matter: their polynomials obey a prescribed matrix-variable symmetry, their circuits are measured by the largest orbit of gates rather than total size, and their symmetric classes have no polynomial degree bound. The symmetry action must extend from input variables to the computation. These classes therefore cannot simply be substituted for the unrestricted classes in this card. The skew class is named symVBP in the January preprint and symVS in the conference abstract. Their additional completeness results for homomorphism polynomials are separate from an unconditional ordinary VP–VBP separation.

The January 2026 report by Fabris, Limaye, Srinivasan and Yehudayoff studies syntactically multilinear ABPs: on each source-to-sink path, a variable appears in at most one affine edge label. It characterizes aspects of a restricted lower-bound measure and recovers a separation of multilinear formulas from multilinear ABPs. Its own introduction still leaves superpolynomial lower bounds for general multilinear ABPs open. In this card even an output that happens to be multilinear may be computed using nonmultilinear intermediate expressions and cancellations. Lower bounds excluding those representations do not establish the unrestricted target.

The size conventions here make the algebraic model explicit. Counting all affine-label occurrences and using binary circuit gates changes customary vertex-only or edge-only presentations by polynomial overhead in the representation size and number of variables. It does not impose bit complexity or uniform constructibility on field constants. A complete answer must preserve these distinctions; a theorem about a min-plus semiring or a fixed-width program would concern different allowed operations or representations.

sentences: VP versus VBP asks whether every polynomial-degree family with small arithmetic circuits also has small algebraic branching programs over the complex numbers.
The branching programs compute exact sums of affine-label products along paths, with all coefficients and variable occurrences included in the algebraic size.
Both models are nonuniform and allow arbitrary complex constants, with no imposed symmetry, width or multilinearity restriction.
A complete Lean-checked answer must establish the universal polynomial simulation or one circuit-easy family requiring superpolynomial branching-program size.
The question would decide whether determinant-like computation captures general efficient algebraic computation, beyond the known quasipolynomial simulations and restricted-model results.
